ox: Incorrect. Extinction means a learned response fades when its reinforcement is removed. Nothing was removed here; the dogs learned their actions did not matter.
Incorrect. Habituation is a decreasing response to a repeated, harmless stimulus. Shocks are not harmless and the dogs did not just get used to them.
Correct. Learned helplessness (Seligman): after uncontrollable aversive events, animals stop trying to escape even when escape is easy.
Incorrect. Social facilitation is improved performance on easy tasks when others are present. No audience is described here.

p: Seligman showed that animals exposed to shocks they could not escape later failed to escape even when escape was easy. The animals learned that outcomes were independent of their actions. It is used as a model for depression and is linked to an external locus of control.

x8A_007.trap: Choosing extinction; nothing was removed, the dogs learned that nothing they do matters.
x8A_007.eli: If the door was locked every time you tried, you stop trying even after someone unlocks it.
mem: Learned helplessness: uncontrollable aversive events → stops trying even when escape is possible (Seligman).
Opposite idea: self-efficacy, believing your actions matter.
x8A_007.sc: 'Could easily avoid but didn't' = learned helplessness.
